newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian shares steady, show few Yeltsin worries.
newsitem.headline: Estonian shares steady, show few Yeltsin worries.

text.p: The Estonian stock exchange shrugged off any worries over Russian President Boris Yeltsin's heart operation on Tuesday, with turnover healthy and the index gaining, dealers said.

Some investors feared instability in Russia and its possible repurcussions in small Estonia if Yeltsin's operation was a failure but analysts said most investors believe Russia's reforms would survive.
"Foreign investors interest (in Estonia) even increased in the last weeks although everybody already knew Yeltsin was to have surgery," said Hansapank analyst Katrin Kaarli.
The market traded 8.1 million kroons on the main list and the Tallinn stock exchange index rose 0.84 per cent to 107.3.
Estonian Forexpank was most traded at four million kroons on the main list and it closed at 76.00 kroons versus 74.85.
"The share price was simply cheap and it attracted interest," Charlie Viikberg, dealer from Estonian Savings Bank, told Reuters.
Savings Bank itself continued its progress to close at 47.80 kroons versus 45.25 turned over one million kroons.
The secondary free market had volume of 4.7 million kroons and the Rakvere meat processer showed trade of 1.5 million kroons and closed slightly higher at six kroons versus 5.75.
